decision.rationale: At the same directed module-boundary II1 and 3 ns synthesis target, the q128 matcher consumes 11.425995x the q16 standard-cell area and 20.391026x the sequential cells. Its raw matcher-issue density is 0.087520x. Even after crediting the eightfold catalog capacity, capacity-normalized issue density is only 0.700158x. Relative to the already prioritized k16/q32 point, q128's exact-work opportunity supplies only a 1.207377x work-bound upper ratio before matcher, PWP storage, DMA, queue and integration costs. This is enough to stop a fully parallel q128 replication line as the current performance path, but not to prove every serialized, hierarchical or workload-specific q128 design is dominated.

findings.title: The M368 shell runner was not in M368's original evidence seal
findings.detail: The current runner hash is frozen by M376 and all current exact-SHA inputs match, but M368's evidence_manifest covers DC outputs rather than the shell runner, input_sha256.txt, copied contract or dc.rc. M376 closes the current snapshot; it cannot retroactively prove which shell-runner bytes launched the historical process.

findings.title: M368 hard-coded the q16 area and froze only q16 RUN_COMPLETE
findings.detail: The 1997.981971 um2 comparator is independently confirmed against M329's full evidence manifest and seal in M376, but M368 itself did not parse that area report or freeze the q16 evidence seal.

findings.title: Raw issue density compares different catalog capacities
findings.detail: The reported 0.0875197x is correct for transactions per cycle per cell area, but q128 searches eight times as many entries as q16. The capacity-normalized ratio is 0.7001579x, so the raw 91.25% loss must not be presented as an equal-functionality density comparison.

findings.title: The area and timing point remains pre-macro and nonphysical
findings.detail: DC used an ideal clock, ZeroWireload, zero macros and reports total area as undefined because net area is absent. There is no placed clock tree, routed interconnect, physical pattern/PWP SRAM, DMA or queue.

findings.title: No netlist equivalence, PrimeTime, SAIF power or complete-executor admission exists
findings.detail: M363/M364 strongly verify RTL behavior, but M368 has no fresh Formality proof for the mapped netlist, no PrimeTime signoff, no activity-backed power and no finite-queue cycle match. The NO-GO is a mainline resource-prioritization decision, not paper PPA or system-speedup evidence.
